title: Car Parking for Private Houses under QCVN 01:2026: 1.2 Spaces per House
desc: QCVN 01:2026 from 2027 sets at least 1.2 car spaces per new-development private house and 1.5 for houses with a shop. How it applies and what buyers should ask.
summary: The minimum car parking ratio for newly developed private houses under QCVN 01:2026/BXD, how parking space is converted to area, and points to note when buying a house in a project.
body: p

Private cars are increasingly common, but many neighbourhoods have nowhere to park them. QCVN 01:2026/BXD (issued with Circular 46/2026/TT-BXD, effective from 1 January 2027) sets car parking ratios for newly developed private houses.
h2
1. The new ratios: 1.2 and 1.5 spaces per house
p
Under Table 19 at section 2.8.4.13, the minimum number of car parking spaces for a building follows the regulation for each type of building; where none exists, the following applies:
ul
Private house group (new development): 1.2 spaces per house;
Private house with a shop (new development): 1.5 spaces per house;
Apartment buildings and mixed-use apartment buildings: under QCVN 04:2021/BXD and Amendment 01:2026;
Hotels of 3 stars and above: 1 space per 4 rooms; premium offices, shopping centres, hospitals: 1 space per 100 m² of usable floor area.
h2
2. Who does it apply to?
p

The ratio applies to private house groups in new development, that is, newly planned urban areas and residential areas. The detailed plan must contain a parking scheme that ensures enough for the planned functions, and the scheme is checked at appraisal (note 3 to Table 19). In urban areas, residential units and house groups must provide parking spaces and parking lots (section 2.8.4.1).
ul
If it cannot be provided within the premises, it may be provided at another location no more than 400 m from the building (note 2 to Table 19).
Pedestrian-priority areas: parking demand is calculated specifically in the zoning plan or detailed plan, not necessarily by Table 19 (note 4).
Detailed plans and designs for renovation, regeneration and redevelopment must provide enough parking within the land area (section 2.8.4.9).
h2
3. Detailed plans must study parking
p

Under section 1.5.5.11, a detailed plan must calculate parking demand and choose a scheme of parking lots and spaces – elevated, at ground level or underground, in public, semi-public and private space – ensuring enough parking for residents and for the buildings in the area.
h2
4. How much area does one parking space need?
p
When converting the number of spaces into area, the standard for one passenger car space is (note 1 to Table 18, section 2.8.4.12):
ul
Ground-level parking lot: 25 m² per space;
Multi-storey and underground parking: 30 m² per space (one level); 20 m² (two levels); 14 m² (three levels); 12 m² (four levels); 10 m² (five levels or more).
p
A standalone car park must provide electric-vehicle charging posts or stations, ensuring fire and explosion safety (section 2.8.4.10).
h2
5. Does an indoor garage count towards the land use coefficient?
p

The land use coefficient is calculated on total floor area but excludes parking floor area, technical floors, fire-fighting areas and refuge areas (section 1.4.22). So the garage part is not counted towards the 7-times land use coefficient limit for a private house plot, but it still counts towards the building footprint and must conform to the construction permit.
h2
6. What should buyers in a project ask?
ol
Where does the project's detailed plan place parking: within each house, in a central car park or in a basement?
How far is the parking from the house (no more than 400 m if outside the premises)?
Is the parking space privately owned, jointly owned or leased?
Does the house design have enough ground-floor width and depth to bring a car in?
note

This article is only a summary for reference and does not replace the legal texts. QCVN 01:2026/BXD takes effect from 1 January 2027; the Table 19 ratios apply when there is no separate regulation for the type of building. QCVN 04:2021/BXD and Amendment 01:2026 are not yet in our library.
